data.description:
## Goal
As a proxy operator, a request handled by the proxy must never be held to (or past) a client's 900-second queue-timeout deadline by a proxy-level wait that sits exactly at 900 s.

## Acceptance criteria (final)
- [x] A single total wall-clock budget bounds ALL chain-hold waits across cycles (streaming + non-streaming) strictly below 900 s (new server.chain_hold_total_seconds, default 720; 0 disables the cap).
- [x] The local dispatch initial first-byte wait is bounded strictly below 900 s by a dedicated knob (new server.local_dispatch_first_byte_timeout_seconds, default 840) so the proxy returns a retryable 503 before the client's 900 s deadline; the lifetime wedge bound (local_dispatch_max_prefill_seconds, 900) is unchanged so healthy long streams keep their full window.
- [x] Config validation: chain_hold_total_seconds negative/non-numeric rejected; values >= 900 rejected (they recreate the exact race).
- [x] Unit tests: cumulative holds never exceed the total budget (non-streaming + streaming), zero total disables the cap, first-byte default < 900; golden config fixtures + BASE_ONLY_SERVER_KEYS updated.
- [x] Docs updated (proxy/config.yaml comments, proxy/docs/remote-fallback-timeout-budget.md).

## Audit context
LP-0MU1S617L002Q9PR audit (2026-10-12) found AC1 'partial': 'the bounded chain-hold can still hold a request up to 300 s x 3 = 900 s (proxy/config.yaml:585,589), with 10 residual ceiling=900 s holds'. The chain hold loop (provider.py _run_chain_cycles / _build_streaming_hold_response) held up to chain_hold_seconds(300) x chain_hold_max_cycles(3) = 900 s, and the local first-byte wait reused the 900 s lifetime knob (dispatch_first_byte_timeout ... ceiling=900s). Both sat exactly at the client deadline.
data.title: Bound chain-hold and local-dispatch ceilings strictly below the client's 900 s deadline (AC1)

data.description:
## Goal
Provide the evidence the LP-0MU1S617L002Q9PR audit requires to close AC1 and AC2; both are measurement / decision items rather than implementation.

## Scope
1. AC1: capture a 24 h post-change window proving no request returns the upstream 900-second queue-timeout error (requires the AC1 ceiling fixes to be deployed first). Instrument/verify via proxy logs (dispatch_first_byte_timeout, chain-hold exhaustion events, and client-reported queue-timeout errors).
2. AC2: produce a fresh dispatch_first_byte_ms breakdown for local-routed requests and recommend how to satisfy 'p99 < 60 s' — either a performance fix or an operator-approved re-scope (e.g. exclude cold full-prefill / slot-wait segments, or set a realistic 1-slot target). Post-deploy artifact (2026-10-12) shows median 8.0 s / p90 80.4 s with a 900 s ceiling tail; ~200 tok/s prompt eval makes large cold prefills inherently tens of seconds.

## Decision required (producer)
Re-scoping AC2 or asserting the 24 h window start/end for AC1.
data.title: AC1 24 h post-change measurement and AC2 first-byte target decision

data.description:
## Goal
Make the re-scoped AC2 measurable: dispatch_first_byte_ms for LOCAL-routed requests is segmented so warm-cache dispatches are identifiable and the single-slot queue wait is separated from service time; the queue wait itself is bounded by the existing contention-queue cap.

## Producer decision (LP-0MV6BR3PT001WBEI, 2026-10-13)
AC2 re-scoped to: warm-cache local dispatches p99 < 60 s to first byte PLUS a queue-wait cap. Cold full-prefill and slot contention are excluded from the warm target; the queue wait stays capped (contention_queue_max_wait_seconds default 60).

## Acceptance criteria (final)
- [x] The dispatch_first_byte_ms log line for local dispatches gains cache_state=warm|cold (cached_ratio >= 0.5 => warm, from provider._get_cached_ratio) and queue_wait_ms (dispatch start -> slot acquired), alongside the existing session/model fields.
- [x] Warm/cold classification is a testable helper with unit tests (ratio threshold; absent ratio => cold; fail-open on provider errors).
- [x] The queue-wait cap is documented as the re-scoped AC2 bound (existing server.contention_queue_max_wait_seconds default 60, already pinned by test_contention_queue.py) and referenced from the metric doc.
- [x] Docs updated (proxy/docs/remote-fallback-timeout-budget.md: re-scoped AC2 measurement surface).
- [x] Full test suite green.

## Audit context
LP-0MU1S617L002Q9PR audit AC2 was 'unmet' (p90 80.4 s / median 8.0 s over 10557 local first-byte samples, tail dominated by single-slot queue wait + cold prefill; the target over ALL local dispatches is unachievable at 1 slot).
data.title: AC2 re-scope: warm-cache first-byte metric with queue-wait split

data.author: pi
data.comment:
Fresh AC2 measurement (proxy logs 2026-10-12 00:00 -> 2026-10-13 07:00 UTC, n=2003 local dispatch_first_byte_ms samples):

- p50 = 7.3 s, p90 = 79.5 s, p99 = 437 s, max = 794 s
- 13.3% of local dispatches exceed 60 s to first byte
- 17 dispatch_first_byte_timeout ceiling=900s events in the window (the AC1 fix lowers this ceiling to 840 s once deployed)

Analysis: the tail is dominated by (1) single-slot queue wait (a local dispatch waits for the in-flight generation on the only slot) and (2) cold full-prefill of large contexts (~200 tok/s prompt eval makes a 40K-token cold prefill ~200 s). A p99 < 60 s target over all local dispatches is not achievable at the 1-slot profile without either queue-wait exclusion or a larger latency envelope.

Recommendation (producer decision): re-scope AC2 to first-byte EXCLUDING the single-slot queue wait (measure from the moment the slot is acquired; the log already emits dispatch_to_first_byte_ms, currently identical — redefine it at the slot boundary), OR split the AC: p99 < 60 s for warm-cache dispatches + a separate cap on queue wait. AC1's new 840 s first-byte ceiling bounds the extreme tail either way.
